operations.new: 3.2 By [L7] and rational density [L9], fix a rational $q>0$ with $\hat q<\varepsilon/(2n)$. For each $j<n$, convergence of its coordinate sequence in step 2.2, as defined in [A1], gives a natural threshold beyond which $|x^{(k)}_j-y_j|<\hat q<\varepsilon/(2n)$. Thus the set of naturals $M$ such that $|x^{(k)}_j-y_j|<\varepsilon/(2n)$ for all $k\ge M$ is nonempty. Let $K_j$ be its least member by [L6], and put $K:=\max\{K_j:j<n\}$, a maximum of a nonempty finite set of naturals since $n\ge1$. [step 2.2, A1, L6, L7, L9, choose]
